issue:
Unicode spaces are stripped when parsing markdown text ``` In [1]: import mistune In [2]: md = mistune.create_markdown(escape=False, hard_wrap=True) In [3]: result = md('\u2003\u2003foo\nbar\n\n\u2003\u2003foobar') In [4]: print(result)

foo
bar

foobar

``` The output is missing the leading em spaces (\u2003) that were in the input text. The expected output should be: ```

\u2003\u2003foo
bar

\u2003\u2003foobar

``` This happens because the text is being stripped with `strip()` which removes all whitespace characters, including unicode spaces like em space. The parser should preserve these special unicode spaces.
